title: The Last Deadline
premise: When Flight 447 to Frankfurt evaporates from every database mid-flight—passenger manifests, air traffic logs, even the memories of the airline's own staff—unattributable analyst Noor Coldharbour is the only investigator whose paper trail can't be traced back to any agency. The vanished flight carries Vesa Lindqvist, a defector holding ledger keys that will detonate or stabilize European markets at Frankfurt's opening bell, and Noor must extract him from a conspiracy that has already rewritten history to erase him. As Noor pieces together the erasure, he discovers the flight never existed at all: Lindqvist is bait, and Noor himself was hired because his ruined reputation makes him the perfect fallible witness. In the end, Noor chooses to publish the true manifest—sacrificing his last shred of anonymity—forcing the conspirators to let the markets open on honest numbers, and walks away owning, for the first time, a name that is entirely his own.
about_author: Mirabel Galloway spent a decade as a financial journalist in Frankfurt before trading bylines for fiction, and her thrillers are prized for their forensic attention to how institutions forget. She writes under a pen name she refuses to confirm, insisting that a book should be the only identity a reader needs.

chapters.title: Unattributed
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Burned out and bounced from three agencies, Noor works deniable cases from a Rotterdam safehouse, introduced mid-job scrubbing a diplomat's digital past. The emotional beat is hollow professionalism—he's become a ghost who edits other people's ghosts, and he knows it.

chapters.title: The Call That Wasn't Logged
chapters.summary: POV Noor. A broker with no name offers Noor a contract: verify that Flight 447, currently airborne to Frankfurt, is carrying defector Vesa Lindqvist. Noor checks and finds the flight exists—until it doesn't. Beat: the first cold spike of fear as reality edits itself in front of him.

chapters.title: Manifest of Nobody
chapters.summary: POV alternating Noor and Ilse Brandt, a Frankfurt exchange regulator. Every record of 447 has vanished—booking systems, radar archives, even crew rosters—yet the plane is still squawking on approach. Beat: vertigo; the two investigators realize they may be the only people who remember it.

chapters.title: Ilse Remembers the Coffee
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse interviewed Lindqvist weeks ago under a different name and now finds her own notes altered. Her memory is the last uncorrupted record, and she's terrified of what that makes her. Beat: intimate dread—identity as evidence, and evidence as a target.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, Zero Alibis
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor's old handlers deny everything, but one slips him a phrase—'Coldharbour protocol'—suggesting he was groomed for exactly this kind of deniable crisis. Beat: bitter recognition that his disposability was always the point.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Never Boarded
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor tracks a 447 passenger's widow who insists her husband never flew, though his suitcase arrived. Inside: a burner phone with one contact—Lindqvist. Beat: grief weaponized; Noor sees how thoroughly the conspiracy has colonized private memory.

chapters.title: Ledger Keys
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse decodes Lindqvist's old filings: he carries cryptographic keys to a decade of falsified clearing-house trades that could crater Frankfurt at open. Beat: the stakes crystallize—this is memory as money, and someone is buying the past.

chapters.title: Approach Vector
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The ghost-flight lands at a closed military strip outside Rotterdam; ground crews behave as if the runway is empty. Noor witnesses Lindqvist escorted off by men with no insignia. Beat: awe curdling into urgency—he has hours, not days.

chapters.title: Coldharbour Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Noor, flashback-heavy. Noor reconstructs his own recruitment and realizes his three firings were staged placements, building a legend of failure. Beat: identity crisis—he cannot trust a single memory of his own career, including his name.

chapters.title: The Widow's Second Suitcase
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse finds the widow dead, staged as suicide, and the second suitcase gone. She chooses to go off-grid and find Noor, trusting a stranger because he's the only stranger left. Beat: reluctant alliance, two ghosts shaking hands.

chapters.title: Extraction Is a Word for Theft
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor infiltrates the holding site where Lindqvist is being 'debriefed'—actually being coerced to surrender the keys before open. Beat: cold competence masking panic; the clock to Frankfurt's opening bell starts ticking in earnest.

chapters.title: Lindqvist, Speaking
chapters.summary: POV Lindqvist. The defector's own chapter: he reveals he volunteered as bait, because only his public extraction will force the conspirators to move their money and expose the ledger. Beat: unsettling charisma—he's playing everyone, including his rescuer.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor realizes the anonymous broker hired him precisely because a failed, unattributable analyst is the perfect scapegoat for a botched extraction. Beat: the trap closes; betrayal lands not as surprise but as the confirmation of every fear about himself.

chapters.title: Night of the Open Bell
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Pre-market Frankfurt hums; Ilse races to freeze suspicious clearing accounts while her own credentials are revoked in real time. Beat: desperate, procedural adrenaline—bureaucracy as a battlefield.

chapters.title: Runway Lights
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor and Lindqvist flee the site through fog and drone surveillance; Lindqvist is wounded. Noor must decide whether the defector is cargo, ally, or the trap itself. Beat: loyalty tested under fire; trust as a calculated gamble.

chapters.title: The Erasure Machine
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Captured briefly, Noor meets the architect: a clearing-house insider who explains the flight was never real—only a synthetic record designed to launder the keys' provenance. Beat: intellectual horror; the conspiracy isn't hiding history, it's manufacturing it.

chapters.title: What Noor Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Interrogated with his own fabricated personnel files, Noor nearly accepts the invented version of himself—until Ilse's voice on a smuggled phone anchors him to the one memory that was never in any database: the day he chose this work. Beat: identity reclaimed from the inside.

chapters.title: Publish the Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Ilse and Noor. Their countermove: release the true passenger manifest and the ledger keys simultaneously, making the conspiracy's fiction public before the bell. Beat: audacious clarity—the only weapon against manufactured memory is witnessed truth.

chapters.title: Opening Bell
chapters.summary: POV multiple, rapid cuts. Frankfurt opens on honest numbers; markets wobble but hold as the ledger detonates selectively, burning the conspirators' own positions. Lindqvist, his purpose served, vanishes into a new identity. Beat: cathartic chaos resolving into fragile order.

chapters.title: The Architect's Last Edit
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The architect attempts one final erasure—Noor himself—and fails, because Noor has already filed his testimony with forty independent outlets under his real name. Beat: quiet triumph; the fallible witness becomes the unerasable one.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Aftermath: agencies disavow, the broker is exposed, and Noor's name is now attached to the story everywhere. He loses the invisibility that defined him and finds he can breathe. Beat: bittersweet liberation—being seen as the price of being real.

chapters.title: The Next Deadline
chapters.summary: POV Noor, coda. Weeks later, Noor receives a new anonymous offer—and declines it, then opens his own one-room consultancy, taking cases people will admit to needing. A final postcard from Lindqvist arrives unsigned. Beat: resolved but alive; memory, inheritance, and identity finally in balance.
